objectClass.primaryType: standing adult male domestic fowl (Thai fighting cock / gai chon)
motionPotential: none - authored as one fixed standing pose; the thaikit kit is static geometry with no rig and no animation
materialFamilies: feather keratin (dielectric, matte to satin, structural-colour sheen)
objectClass.notes: Living figure, so proportion, stance and every left/right pair are identity-defining, but NOT a human: the character profile's landmark gates are MediaPipe face and pose extractors that have nothing to say about a bird. Built on the generic profile with primaryDomain hybrid; the chirality gate and the swept-arc gate are turned on by hand in their place. A gai chon is distinguished from a farmyard rooster by a DRESSED comb (a low papillated ridge with no serrated points), a trimmed wattle, bare red face and upper neck, a long exposed tarsus, an erect neck carriage and a slim close-feathered body -- all confirmed against the plate at high zoom, not assumed from the name.

reasoning: Silhouette 8: the outline is carried by a swept tail arc, an erect neck and a long tarsus, none of which a primitive reproduces. A straight cone occupies roughly the right silhouette cells, which is exactly why the swept-arc gate is required here.
Occlusion 8: one lateral view. The far wing, the far leg's spur, the back of the head, the tail's lateral spread and the whole underside are hidden.
Repetition 8: the tail is a shingled stack of ~14 feather cards, there are 8 claws and 2 spurs. Instancing these is what keeps the prop inside 24 draw calls.
ActionReadiness 2: nothing on this prop articulates. One root pivot, no sockets, no destruction groups -- the low score is the correct answer, not a gap.
Tier complex rather than ultra-complex: the form is demanding but there is no printed graphic, no pattern to register against a reference and no finish system.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed, not assumed from a domain profile: four macro assemblies (head-and-neck, body-and-wings, legs, tail), sixteen meso parts, and three repetition systems the draw-call ceiling makes mandatory rather than optional. Action-ready hierarchy is required for explodability and click-selection only -- the prop has no moving parts.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Low papillated fore-aft ridge on the crown with NO serrated points -- the comb has been trimmed. Stands proud of the crown, never in-plane with it.
A single small fleshy nub under the jaw where an untrimmed rooster carries two hanging lobes.
Bare crimson skin over the face, throat and upper neck, meeting the hackle mantle at an abrupt line rather than fading into it.
Stout horn beak, upper mandible overhanging the lower in a hook; the culmen carries a satin sheen.

Neck carried near-vertical from the shoulder, not in a farmyard S-curve. Measured: above 0.80 of height the silhouette depth collapses from 0.602 to 0.139 of height, which is the neck standing clear of the body.
Exposed scaled tarsus running from 0.05 to 0.36 of standing height -- 0.17 m of bare leg on a 0.55 m bird.
Dark plumage stops at a hard horizontal line at the hock and pale scale begins. A boundary, not a gradient.

mapsTo.note: component:thigh-l/-r lower edge vs tarsus top

details.description: A short conical spur on the medial aspect of each tarsus, pointing aft and slightly inward.

A shingled stack of long pale feathers arching aft and DOWN along a curve; the two longest sickles curl furthest. Aft-most point of the whole silhouette sits at 0.60 of height, so the tail rises before it falls -- a straight fan is wrong.
Pale grey-brown feathers with irregular dark flecking and a visible central rachis. Measured luma contrast within one crop is 125 (P10 31, P90 156) -- the highest local contrast anywhere on the bird.
Deep oxblood hackle cape over the lower neck and an oxblood saddle over the lower back, both against a near-black body.
Teal-green structural-colour sheen on the covert tips of the wing and shoulder. Measured as a low-saturation sheen (rgb 40,37,32), not a metallic response.
No loose fluff at the flank; the body shell is tight and slim. Peak body band width is 0.274 of height against a 0.304 foot-stance width.
One foot planted forward of the other by roughly 0.05 m; the stance is not a symmetric two-foot plant.
Three forward toes and one aft hallux per foot, each ending in a pale horn claw.

pose.note: One fixed pose. No rig, no animation, no articulation anywhere on this prop.

anatomy.note:
MEASURED BY HAND OFF THE PLATE, NOT EXTRACTED. extract_landmarks.py was deliberately not run: it is a MediaPipe face and pose extractor built for humans and it has nothing to say about a bird, so its output here would be numbers with nothing behind them. Every value above is a real measurement of the avian analogue of the field that holds it, and each is stated so that a reader can check it rather than trust it:
  headUnit 0.045 m = crown 0.550 minus head base 0.505.
  styleHeads 12.22 = standing height in those head units. A bird is not 8 heads tall.
  torso 4.71 = body vertical extent 0.212 m (back 0.406 to belly 0.194) in head units.
  legs 3.67 = ground to crotch 0.165 m in head units.
  shoulderWidth 2.27 / hipWidth 2.22 = lateral widths from the reference GLB's band profile, the one axis a single lateral view cannot measure. These two carry that proxy's 0.5 confidence.
  eyeLine 0.422 = crown to pupil (0.550 - 0.531) in head units. The pupil is the centroid of the 99 plate pixels below luma 45 in the eye window, not an estimate by eye.
  eyeSpacing 0.943 = eye separation 0.033 m over head width 0.035 m. A bird's eyes are LATERAL, which is why this is near 1.0 where a human's is near 0.4 -- the number is doing real work, not filling a slot.
  noseBase 0.609 = crown to the NOSTRIL on the upper mandible, the avian analogue of a nose base.
  mouthLine 0.762 = crown to the GAPE, where the mandibles meet.
  hairline 0.089 = crown to the comb's base on the skull -- where bare skin gives way to the comb, the nearest thing this animal has to a hairline.
The two gates that DO apply to a living non-human figure, chirality and swept-arc, are turned on by hand in the review contract; the character track's likeness and landmark gates are not run and must not be.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolvedNote: Every unknown this single lateral view raised is RESOLVED, not open, so this list is empty by the schema's meaning of it -- 'unknowns to resolve before implementation'. Each resolution, its method and its confidence is recorded verbatim in spec.unknownsDetail and restated in spec.assumptions. Six of the seven are resolved by mirroring or by the reference GLB and carry confidences of 0.40 to 0.60; that low confidence is the honest number and is not hidden by the empty list above.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every component is a named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, so the model is explodable and clickable. That is the whole of the action requirement here.
actionReadiness.movingPartsNote: THIS PROP HAS NO MOVING PARTS. It is authored in one fixed standing pose, and thaikit's kit is static geometry with no rig and no animation. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on that axis and a named socket is a promise that something attaches there; a bird that declared a pivot per joint because a live bird has one would have described a machine that does not exist. So: ONE pivot, the root at base-center, and ZERO sockets. That is the correct answer, not a gap.

pivots.note: base-center, on the ground at the centroid of the two foot contact patches

actionReadiness.destructionNote: The asset declares NO destruction groups. Nothing anywhere in this spec sets a fractureGroup.

assumptions: The plate is the bird's left flank with the camera at +X. One view cannot establish which flank; fixed by convention so chirality has something to measure against.
The far wing, the far leg's spur and the back of the head are mirrored from the near side. Confidence 0.55-0.60.
Lateral tail spread is taken from the reference GLB's band profile, a generative proxy. Confidence 0.50.
Breast frontal width is taken as 0.60 of the body's fore-aft length. A lateral view cannot show it. Confidence 0.50.

The stance is built MIRROR-SYMMETRIC with both feet at z = 0 and the toes splayed outward, where the plate shows one foot about 40 mm forward of the other. The offset is recorded in the detail inventory as NOT identity-defining, and a symmetric stance both satisfies the chirality gate cleanly and gives a level builder a neutral prop. This is a deliberate, recorded deviation from the plate, not an oversight.
The pale amber iris ring is knowingly omitted at about 4 mm on a 0.55 m prop.

PLUMAGE PASS (2026-08-27, post-ship, user-reported 'smooth and shiny, not organic'): every feathered surface now carries a seeded seamless Canvas 2D tile bound post-construction as map+bumpMap (contour feathers 120 mm tile, lanceolate hackle 80 mm, pencilled pale tail 100 mm, tarsus scutes 30 mm, papillated head skin 30 mm), so every material stays declared textureless and the measured albedo is the tile's re-based mean. Tone spreads are plate ratios (hackle p5/p95 0.29/1.71, pale tail 0.57/2.09, tarsus 0.67/1.37, head skin 0.46/1.59) with the dark ends lifted for the luma-58 hole gate. Cost: 84 ms for all five tiles at 256 px on the CPU canvas path (willReadFrequently) -- the same drawing on the GPU-backed canvas cost 2.3 s under SwiftShader. 1.7 MB texture VRAM.

The SDF-polygonised meshes carry no uv, so the body is mapped cylindrically about the VERTICAL axis (a mapping about z put its pole on the breast, which rendered as a pinwheel) and the legs conically about the tarsus so scute rows run down the toes; the tapered sweeps' 0..1 uv is rescaled to metres from ring perimeter and path length.

The neck column is on plumage-oxblood, not skin-red: the plate's neck crop (720,160) is rgb 63/21/18, the hackle's own colour, against head skin at 123/71/65. Only the face and throat are bare, and those are the head's geometry.

Body smooth-union radius raised 0.03 -> 0.05 and polygonizer resolution 24 -> 36 (the five ellipsoids read as separate lobes at 0.03), with the SDF bounds padded 17-20 mm: at the original tight bounds the blended surface crossed the box and the body shipped as an open C-shell. Tapered sweeps are subdivided 3x through a centripetal Catmull-Rom (positions and radii) so the wings and sickles are no longer creased at each authored station. Triangles 20,732 -> 26,032 of 32,000; materials 10 -> 7 (the SDF meshes' duplicate createSculptMaterial instances now share materialMap's). Band table after: mean |depth error| 0.0551 of height over 19 bands against 0.0538 recorded at ship.

Feathered materials gained a low sheen lobe (body 0.18 teal, hackle 0.28 oxblood, tail 0.15) and went a step rougher (0.45 -> 0.62 body, 0.48 -> 0.58 hackle): at sheen 0.55 the whole body rendered green. Wing coverts and shoulder carry a low-frequency vertex tint (teal 0.78/1.0/0.95 linear, oxblood 1.18/0.9/0.85) on white-filled colour attributes across every plumage-dark geometry.

ANATOMY PASS (2026-08-27, user: 'looks like it's made of wood; no curve in the neck; legs not straight; head shape and eye wrong'). Rebuilt to plate landmarks (1 px = 0.625 mm, origin at the tarsus): neck is a six-station curve from (y 0.35, z 0.029) through (0.445, 0.061) and (0.515, 0.097) into the skull, radii 37 -> 13 mm, with the hackle cape following it to y 0.506 and tapering INTO the neck instead of ending in a ring; drumsticks are vertical (hip root x 0.024 straight down to the hock at 0.030 -- they walked 20 mm outward before and read knock-kneed); head node moved to the plate eye (0.531, 0.112), skull re-authored as a domed wedge 33 x 42 x 58 mm with a small nape, a trimmed wattle and a pea comb, beak base at (0.523, 0.126) with the tip at z 0.162 against the plate's 0.166; eyes are 12 mm pearl eyes on a 27 mm ring with a canvas iris (pupil 30 deg, iris 62 deg, absolute colours, drawn at u=0.5 where a SphereGeometry's +x lies); folded wings moved into the flank (x 0.052 -> 0.040, outward radius 14 mm) with the tip walked 14 mm inboard so it is buried rather than spiking out behind. Gate suite all PASS; band table 0.0516 of height (0.0538 at ship). Triangles 27,208 / 32,000.

NECK/HEAD PASS (2026-08-27, user: 'neck still too straight, deepen the S; the head should blend in at the neck -- no bump indicating a large skull'). Neck stations now run up-and-BACK off the shoulders (z 0.037 -> 0.029 over the first 50 mm), forward through the middle (to z 0.093 at y 0.51) and near-vertical into the skull; top ring 23 mm. The skull was moved forward so its rear is tangent to the neck's back line and the nape ellipsoid (33 x 44 x 38 mm, blend 15 mm) IS the neck's continuation -- the previous skull bulged 25 mm behind the neck. A 1 mm sliver where the neck's top ring cut through the skull's side (neck r 14.5 vs skull half-width 13.5 there) is fixed by the narrower top ring. The hackle cape's top station is now fully inside the neck (same material) so it ends without a ledge. Gates 8/8 PASS; band 0.0564 of height; 29,240 / 32,000 triangles.

componentTree.name: Body shell: breast, back, flank and tail base
componentTree.topologyRationale: A bird's trunk is one continuous organic volume with no seam anywhere on it. Seven smooth-unioned ellipsoids give the tilted ovoid the plate shows -- deep breast forward and low, back sloping down aft to the pygostyle -- which no single primitive reproduces. `continuous-sculpt` was the alternative but it forbids exactly the box/cylinder/cone primitives and still needs one lathe axis, and this body has no axis of revolution.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: tilted continuous trunk volume, shoulder-high and forward, vent-low and aft
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Implicit surface at resolution 24 over its own bounds; see resolutionNote for the measured cost.
geometryDescriptor.proportionNote: Measured off the plate, height normalised to 0.55 m: back top y = 0.406, belly y = 0.194, crotch y = 0.165, breast forward z = +0.116, tail root z = -0.083. The body's long axis is tilted about 32 degrees nose-up, which is the upright gamecock carriage.
geometryDescriptor.parentingNote: TRANSFORM PARENT IS THE ROOT for every component; the logical hierarchy lives in attachment.parentId. The generator parents nodes by `component.parent` and COMPOSES their transforms, and most geometry here is authored in world coordinates (both leg fields, the body field) or hung off a world-placed pivot (every sweep). Leaving the logical parent in `parent` would have added the thigh's offset to a leg already at its world position and displaced it by exactly that much. Flattening is the same fix the 7-Eleven's facade wall carries, for the same reason. The model is still fully explodable and clickable: every component is its own named node.
geometryDescriptor.resolutionNote: Resolution 24, about 9.5 mm cells. The body is a smooth blob with NO geometric feature at any scale -- its detail is the scalloped feather edge, which is material. 9.5 mm cells cost about 4,800 triangles where 34 cost 9,560 for a shape no camera can tell apart. Measured, not guessed. A resolution sweep on this exact spec (res_probe.mjs, five builds) gives total triangles 4,672 / 10,516 / 21,000 / 29,456 / 29,456 at resolutions 16 / 24 / 34 / 44 / 52, and factory build times of 169 / 382 / 898 / 1,274 / 1,279 ms. Two things follow. Triangle count goes as the SQUARE of the resolution, so this is the only lever that matters. And it SATURATES at 44: 44 and 52 return identical geometry, because the tessellation tier derived from targetTriangles caps the implicit sampling grid. The 52 and 56 first authored here were therefore never real -- they were clamped, and reading the spec you would have believed otherwise. SOURCE OF THE SATURATION, found in optimization-pass: the sweep showed resolutions 44 and 52 returning identical geometry and I recorded that as 'saturates at 44'. The real number is 40 -- forge/_shared/subdivision.py sets SDF_MAX_RESOLUTION to 40 for the `standard` tessellation tier, which targetTriangles 32000 selects. Both 44 and 52 were being clamped to 40, which is why they agreed. Every resolution on this prop (24, 34, 36) is below the cap and is therefore real.

STRUCTURAL-PASS CORRECTION 1 -- a real defect with a real visual consequence, found by self_intersection and then pinned down by signed volume. These two components were the ONLY ones built from the `capsule` primitive, and they were the only two the gate flagged: 256 of 258 vertices reading as inside their own surface, 99.2%. That is not an intersection, it is INVERTED WINDING. Measured directly: signed volume -7.29e-5 for both thighs against +2.44e-3, +4.52e-4, +1.05e-4 and so on for every other component, and 1% of vertex normals pointing outward against 100% everywhere else. buildWatertightCapsule emits its triangles wound inward. With backface culling that renders the far wall of the limb instead of the near one, which is why the drumstick read as a thin hollow sleeve.
FIX: stop using `capsule` here rather than patch the generated helper -- a patch would be lost on the next regeneration, and img2threejs is a SHARED checkout where an unflagged behaviour change is not mine to make. tapered-sweep is independently the better primitive for a drumstick: a thigh tapers from a thick top to a narrow hock and a capsule cannot. geometryDescriptor.attachmentDepthNote:

The thigh's root sat at world y 0.205, and the body's surface at the thigh's own position -- x 0.030, z 0.006 -- is at about y 0.214, NOT at the 0.1934 its bounding box reports. The box minimum occurs at x=0 on the midline, where the keel ellipsoid hangs lowest; by the time you move 30 mm out to the leg the body has already curved back up. So the boxes 'overlapped by 13.6 mm' while the surfaces barely grazed: measured penetration depth was 6.1 mm on the left thigh and 2.5 mm on the right. Those two numbers are also the proof it was marginal -- the pair is an exact mirror and cannot genuinely differ, so a 6-versus-2 split is a sampling artefact of an overlap too thin to sample reliably. Against a body whose smooth-union blend alone moves its surface by up to 7.5 mm, that is not a joint.
FIX: the root rises from y 0.205 to 0.228 and widens from 0.030 x 0.024 to 0.032 x 0.026, while the sweep lengthens so its tip still lands exactly on the hock at y 0.126. The root is now about 18 mm INSIDE the flank instead of grazing its surface. The drumstick still bulges 8 mm proud of the body laterally, which is what a thigh does.
WHY NO GATE CAUGHT THIS EITHER: nothing in the suite compared two components' SURFACES. The connectivity check added after the detached feet tests whether ONE mesh is one piece, which every mesh was; bounding boxes overlapped, so nothing looked wrong from the outside. An attachment-proximity check that reports a DEPTH now runs over every declared attachment.parentId, and it fails anything joined by less than 2 mm.
geometryDescriptor.capNote:
POST-SHIP CORRECTION 3 -- THE FLAT CAP ON TOP OF THE LEG. Correction 2 buried the thigh root 18 mm into the flank and the joint measured 14-28 mm deep, but a tapered sweep is CAPPED: capEnds puts a flat disc across its first station, and that disc was still partly outside the body. At world y 0.228 the body is only 0.037 wide at the thigh's own z, while the cap reached 0.056, so a crescent of flat plane sat proud of the curved flank and read as a machined face on an organic form -- connected, and still visibly not JOINED.
Two obvious fixes are both wrong. Removing the cap (capEnds false) leaves an open rim whose inner wall is backfacing, so the leg would render see-through at that crescent instead of flat -- worse. Shrinking the root is blocked by the taper rule: tip/root must be at most 0.55 and the hock end is 0.011, so the root cannot go below 0.020.
FIX: move the root INWARD and DEEPER, to where the body is wide enough to swallow it. Sampling the body's own ellipsoids gives a half-width of 0.037 at y 0.228 but 0.040 at y 0.250, so the root rises to y 0.250 and moves in to world x 0.010, where its 0.024 lateral half-extent spans -0.014 to 0.034 -- entirely inside the body's 0.040. Stations carry a local x for the first time on this prop, mirrored through the side sign like everything else, so the pair stays an exact reflection.

geometryDescriptor.correctionNote:
STRUCTURAL-PASS CORRECTION 1 -- a real defect with a real visual consequence, found by self_intersection and then pinned down by signed volume. These two components were the ONLY ones built from the `capsule` primitive, and they were the only two the gate flagged: 256 of 258 vertices reading as inside their own surface, 99.2%. That is not an intersection, it is INVERTED WINDING. Measured directly: signed volume -7.29e-5 for both thighs against +2.44e-3, +4.52e-4, +1.05e-4 and so on for every other component, and 1% of vertex normals pointing outward against 100% everywhere else. buildWatertightCapsule emits its triangles wound inward. With backface culling that renders the far wall of the limb instead of the near one, which is why the drumstick read as a thin hollow sleeve.
FIX: stop using `capsule` here rather than patch the generated helper -- a patch would be lost on the next regeneration, and img2threejs is a SHARED checkout where an unflagged behaviour change is not mine to make. tapered-sweep is independently the better primitive for a drumstick: a thigh tapers from a thick top to a narrow hock and a capsule cannot. This also fixes the measured band error at 0.30 of height, where the plate reads 0.156 of fore-aft extent and the capsule gave 0.067.
geometryDescriptor.frameNote: The spine runs almost straight down, so the parallel-transport frame puts the NORMAL on Z and the BINORMAL on X: here rx is the FORE-AFT half-depth and rz the LATERAL half-width. Root is 0.060 m deep and 0.048 m wide; the hock is 0.026 x 0.022.
geometryDescriptor.taperNote: Tip/root ratio 0.011/0.028 = 0.39, and the section decreases monotonically root to tip.
geometryDescriptor.attachmentDepthNote:
POST-SHIP CORRECTION 2 -- THE LEGS WERE NOT ATTACHED TO THE BODY. Reported by eye, then measured with a new surface-proximity check rather than argued about. The thigh's root sat at world y 0.205, and the body's surface at the thigh's own position -- x 0.030, z 0.006 -- is at about y 0.214, NOT at the 0.1934 its bounding box reports. The box minimum occurs at x=0 on the midline, where the keel ellipsoid hangs lowest; by the time you move 30 mm out to the leg the body has already curved back up. So the boxes 'overlapped by 13.6 mm' while the surfaces barely grazed: measured penetration depth was 6.1 mm on the left thigh and 2.5 mm on the right. Those two numbers are also the proof it was marginal -- the pair is an exact mirror and cannot genuinely differ, so a 6-versus-2 split is a sampling artefact of an overlap too thin to sample reliably. Against a body whose smooth-union blend alone moves its surface by up to 7.5 mm, that is not a joint.
FIX: the root rises from y 0.205 to 0.228 and widens from 0.030 x 0.024 to 0.032 x 0.026, while the sweep lengthens so its tip still lands exactly on the hock at y 0.126. The root is now about 18 mm INSIDE the flank instead of grazing its surface. The drumstick still bulges 8 mm proud of the body laterally, which is what a thigh does.
WHY NO GATE CAUGHT THIS EITHER: nothing in the suite compared two components' SURFACES. The connectivity check added after the detached feet tests whether ONE mesh is one piece, which every mesh was; bounding boxes overlapped, so nothing looked wrong from the outside. An attachment-proximity check that reports a DEPTH now runs over every declared attachment.parentId, and it fails anything joined by less than 2 mm.
geometryDescriptor.capNote:
POST-SHIP CORRECTION 3 -- THE FLAT CAP ON TOP OF THE LEG. Correction 2 buried the thigh root 18 mm into the flank and the joint measured 14-28 mm deep, but a tapered sweep is CAPPED: capEnds puts a flat disc across its first station, and that disc was still partly outside the body. At world y 0.228 the body is only 0.037 wide at the thigh's own z, while the cap reached 0.056, so a crescent of flat plane sat proud of the curved flank and read as a machined face on an organic form -- connected, and still visibly not JOINED.
Two obvious fixes are both wrong. Removing the cap (capEnds false) leaves an open rim whose inner wall is backfacing, so the leg would render see-through at that crescent instead of flat -- worse. Shrinking the root is blocked by the taper rule: tip/root must be at most 0.55 and the hock end is 0.011, so the root cannot go below 0.020.
FIX: move the root INWARD and DEEPER, to where the body is wide enough to swallow it. Sampling the body's own ellipsoids gives a half-width of 0.037 at y 0.228 but 0.040 at y 0.250, so the root rises to y 0.250 and moves in to world x 0.010, where its 0.024 lateral half-extent spans -0.014 to 0.034 -- entirely inside the body's 0.040. The sweep then walks back OUT to x 0.030 as it descends, so the drumstick still emerges from the flank and lands on the tarsus at the hock. Stations carry a local x for the first time on this prop, mirrored through the side sign like everything else, so the pair stays an exact reflection.

attachment.note: Buried into the flank; only the segment below the body contour is visible. No gap is permitted: gapTolerance 0.5 mm, and the joint is an embed so no two faces are coincident and co-facing.

componentTree.topologyRationale: Tarsus, four toes, four claws and the spur are ONE continuous keratinised surface in life, not parts bolted together, so they are one implicit field smooth-unioned from fourteen primitives. geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: continuous scaled leg: tarsometatarsus, ankle, three forward toes sloping to the ground, an aft hallux, five horn points -- ONE connected surface
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Implicit surface at resolution 36 over its own bounds; see resolutionNote for the measured cost.
geometryDescriptor.chiralityNote: A reflection of leg-r. Every primitive's x negates and the toe splay angle psi negates with it, so the toes fan outward on both sides instead of both fanning the same way -- which is the defect medial_lateral_bias exists to catch.
geometryDescriptor.parentingNote: TRANSFORM PARENT IS THE ROOT for every component; the logical hierarchy lives in attachment.parentId. The generator parents nodes by `component.parent` and COMPOSES their transforms, and most geometry here is authored in world coordinates (both leg fields, the body field) or hung off a world-placed pivot (every sweep). Leaving the logical parent in `parent` would have added the thigh's offset to a leg already at its world position and displaced it by exactly that much. Flattening is the same fix the 7-Eleven's facade wall carries, for the same reason. The model is still fully explodable and clickable: every component is its own named node.
geometryDescriptor.resolutionNote: Resolution 36, about 4.0 mm cells. Held higher again: the toes are 10 mm across and the claws 8.8 mm, so 4.0 mm cells give a toe 2.5 cells. That is the floor before the implicit union fuses three toes into a paddle, and it is checked by eye on the render rather than assumed. Measured, not guessed. A resolution sweep on this exact spec (res_probe.mjs, five builds) gives total triangles 4,672 / 10,516 / 21,000 / 29,456 / 29,456 at resolutions 16 / 24 / 34 / 44 / 52, and factory build times of 169 / 382 / 898 / 1,274 / 1,279 ms. Two things follow. Triangle count goes as the SQUARE of the resolution, so this is the only lever that matters. And it SATURATES at 44: 44 and 52 return identical geometry, because the tessellation tier derived from targetTriangles caps the implicit sampling grid. The 52 and 56 first authored here were therefore never real -- they were clamped, and reading the spec you would have believed otherwise. SOURCE OF THE SATURATION, found in optimization-pass: the sweep showed resolutions 44 and 52 returning identical geometry and I recorded that as 'saturates at 44'. The real number is 40 -- forge/_shared/subdivision.py sets SDF_MAX_RESOLUTION to 40 for the `standard` tessellation tier, which targetTriangles 32000 selects. Both 44 and 52 were being clamped to 40, which is why they agreed. Every resolution on this prop (24, 34, 36) is below the cap and is therefore real.
geometryDescriptor.connectivityNote:
POST-SHIP CORRECTION -- THE FEET WERE NOT ATTACHED. Reported by eye, then confirmed as a topology measurement rather than an impression: welding vertices by position and counting connected components gave leg-l and leg-r TWO islands each, 867 vertices of tarsus and 754 of foot, where all fourteen other components are a single island.
CAUSE: the ankle sphere sat at y 0.047 with radius 0.0085, bottoming out at 0.0385, while the toe capsules lay flat at y 0.011 with radius 0.005, topping out at 0.016. A 22.5 mm gap, against a smooth-union radius of 4.5 mm. The field never joined them, so marching cubes correctly produced two surfaces -- the toes were floating 22 mm below the leg.
WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, which matters more than the fix: self_intersection tests whether a surface folds through ITSELF, not whether it is one piece, and it passed at 0 of 9,832 vertices. turntable_gate would have seen enclosed background, but it is run with --allow-holes because a standing bird legitimately encloses background between its legs, and that waiver covered this too. check_part_coverage counts parts, not connectivity. The defect sat exactly in the blind spot all three share, which is why a connectivity check is now part of the gate suite.
FIX: the toes no longer lie flat. Each roots INSIDE the ankle sphere at (x0, 0.033, +/-0.002) -- 3.2 mm from its centre, well within the 9.5 mm radius -- and runs forward and DOWN at 30 degrees to rest its tip on the ground, which is also what the plate shows: the foot spreads from about y 0.045 down to the ground over roughly 0.09 m of reach. The ankle drops to y 0.036 and grows to 9.5 mm, the tarsus segment now ends ON the ankle centre rather than 11 mm above it, and the hallux droops 50 degrees aft-down instead of lying flat. Union radius 4.5 -> 5.5 mm. Every change is mirrored through the side sign alone, so the pair stays a true reflection.
geometryDescriptor.groundContactNote: The leg field is authored in world coordinates and the node then drops it 2.53 mm, which is exactly the clearance the built model measured between the lowest toe vertex and y = 0. A floor prop whose declared origin is 'on the ground plane at the centroid of the two foot contact patches' must actually TOUCH that plane; at 2.5 mm the bird hovered, and in a level builder that reads as a placement bug rather than as a modelling one. The thigh-to-tarsus overlap absorbs the drop -- it was 7.6 mm and is now 5.1 mm, so the joint stays welded.
geometryDescriptor.hockJointNote: The tarsus capsule's segment now runs y 0.037 to 0.137 (caps to 0.030-0.144) rather than stopping at 0.126. Measured at 4.1 and 3.8 mm for a MIRRORED pair, the old hock joint was thin enough that the two sides sampled differently, which is the signature of a marginal overlap. The tarsus now runs 18 mm up inside the drumstick, where the thigh's section is 0.0135 against the tarsus's 0.0068, so it is comfortably enclosed.

attachment.note: Butts against the drumstick at the hock. The faces there are OPPOSED, which is how solids are meant to meet; the thigh capsule also overlaps the tarsus top by 4 mm. No gap is permitted: gapTolerance 0.5 mm, and the joint is an butt so no two faces are coincident and co-facing.

componentTree.name: Shingled pale tail fan
componentTree.topologyRationale: The tail's main mass is a shingled stack of overlapping feathers that reads as one laterally-wide, dorsoventrally-thin sheaf at prop distance. Built as one swept shell along the tail's measured arc, laterally wide and thin through, tapering to a point.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: swept sheaf of tail feathers arching aft and up, then curling aft and down
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 13 stations x 14 radial segments, capped: about 364 triangles.
geometryDescriptor.sweptArcNote: THE arc claim on this prop. Measured off the plate: tail root at world (y 0.300, z -0.083); the tail's highest point at (y 0.453, z -0.189); the aft-most point of the WHOLE silhouette at (y 0.338, z -0.303). The spine rises 0.092 m before it falls, so it is NOT monotonic. A straight cone from root to tip occupies roughly the right silhouette cells and is completely wrong, which is the case swept_arc_gate.py exists for.
geometryDescriptor.sectionNote: rx (in-plane) runs 0.030 -> 0.054 -> 0 and rz (lateral) stays between 0.024 and 0.011, so the fan is roughly TWICE as deep in profile as it is wide across. That is the right anisotropy for a rooster's tail, which spreads in the sagittal plane and stays narrow seen from behind.
geometryDescriptor.taperNote: Tip closes to a true point, ratio 0.
geometryDescriptor.parentingNote: TRANSFORM PARENT IS THE ROOT for every component; the logical hierarchy lives in attachment.parentId. The generator parents nodes by `component.parent` and COMPOSES their transforms, and most geometry here is authored in world coordinates (both leg fields, the body field) or hung off a world-placed pivot (every sweep). Leaving the logical parent in `parent` would have added the thigh's offset to a leg already at its world position and displaced it by exactly that much. Flattening is the same fix the 7-Eleven's facade wall carries, for the same reason. The model is still fully explodable and clickable: every component is its own named node.
geometryDescriptor.frameNote: FRAME SEMANTICS, read out of buildTaperedSweepGeometry rather than assumed. The sweep uses a PARALLEL-TRANSPORT frame: `rx` scales the frame's NORMAL and `rz` its BINORMAL. For a spine that lies wholly in the YZ plane, as both tail sweeps and the neck do, the seed reference (0,0,1) transports to a normal inside the sagittal plane and a binormal of exactly (1,0,0). So for this prop `rx` is the IN-PLANE (profile) half-thickness and `rz` is the LATERAL half-width -- the opposite way round from what the first draft of this spec claimed. The first blockout render is what exposed it: the tail read broad in profile and narrow from behind, which is the right answer arrived at from a wrong description, and a description that would have sent the next correction in exactly the wrong direction.
geometryDescriptor.correctionNote: form-refinement correction 2. Band 0.80 of height was the WORST band in the structural review at -0.479: the plate carries 0.598 of fore-aft extent at y 0.44 and the model carried 0.119, because the tail crossed that height as a narrow tube and left it again. The plate's tail is broad there because its arc runs NEAR-HORIZONTAL across the crest for a long stretch while a fan of feathers spreads along it. The Bezier control points are re-chosen so the spine flattens across its crest instead of turning a corner, and the in-plane radius at the crest goes 0.054 -> 0.058 for the fan. Station count 11 -> 13 to keep the flatter curve from faceting.
geometryDescriptor.smoothingNote: blockout correction 3. The six-station arc rendered as a faceted polygonal slab with visible creases, because buildTaperedSweepGeometry joins stations with STRAIGHT segments -- it does not spline between them, so station count IS the curve's resolution. Resampled to eleven stations along a cubic Bezier through the three measured points (root, crest, tip). The cost was measured rather than assumed: stations x radialSegments x 2, so 11 x 14 x 2 = 308 triangles for the fan against the 15,748 already spent on the implicit surfaces.
geometryDescriptor.crestNote: Crest spine now sits at world y 0.3977 and holds within 10 mm of that height over roughly a third of the sweep's length.

attachment.note: Root station sits inside the pygostyle lobe of the body shell. No gap is permitted: gapTolerance 0.5 mm, and the joint is an embed so no two faces are coincident and co-facing.

localFeatures.description: Irregular dark flecking over a pale grey-brown ground. Measured luma contrast within a single crop is 125 (P10 31, P90 156) -- the highest local contrast anywhere on the bird.
Feathers overlap in a shingled stack; carried by the sheaf's flattened section.

geometryDescriptor.taperNote: Tip closes to a true point, ratio 0.
geometryDescriptor.parentingNote: TRANSFORM PARENT IS THE ROOT for every component; the logical hierarchy lives in attachment.parentId. The generator parents nodes by `component.parent` and COMPOSES their transforms, and most geometry here is authored in world coordinates (both leg fields, the body field) or hung off a world-placed pivot (every sweep). Leaving the logical parent in `parent` would have added the thigh's offset to a leg already at its world position and displaced it by exactly that much. Flattening is the same fix the 7-Eleven's facade wall carries, for the same reason. The model is still fully explodable and clickable: every component is its own named node.
geometryDescriptor.frameNote: FRAME SEMANTICS, read out of buildTaperedSweepGeometry rather than assumed. The sweep uses a PARALLEL-TRANSPORT frame: `rx` scales the frame's NORMAL and `rz` its BINORMAL. For a spine that lies wholly in the YZ plane, as both tail sweeps and the neck do, the seed reference (0,0,1) transports to a normal inside the sagittal plane and a binormal of exactly (1,0,0). So for this prop `rx` is the IN-PLANE (profile) half-thickness and `rz` is the LATERAL half-width -- the opposite way round from what the first draft of this spec claimed. The first blockout render is what exposed it: the tail read broad in profile and narrow from behind, which is the right answer arrived at from a wrong description, and a description that would have sent the next correction in exactly the wrong direction.
geometryDescriptor.correctionNote: form-refinement correction 4, and the LAST unique-geometry slot on this prop -- it takes the count to 16 of 16. Spent here because bands 0.50 and 0.55 of height were the two worst remaining after the crest fix, at -0.154 and -0.191: the plate carries 0.531 and 0.619 of fore-aft extent at y 0.275 and y 0.303, and the model carried 0.377 and 0.428, because the upper fan's LOWEST point is its tip at y 0.326 and there was simply nothing below it. In the plate a second group of feathers hangs aft and down from the coverts and fills exactly that space. One sweep has one spine and cannot occupy both, so this is the case for a second component rather than a wider first one.
geometryDescriptor.smoothingNote: blockout correction 3. The six-station arc rendered as a faceted polygonal slab with visible creases, because buildTaperedSweepGeometry joins stations with STRAIGHT segments -- it does not spline between them, so station count IS the curve's resolution. Resampled to eleven stations along a cubic Bezier through the three measured points (root, crest, tip). The cost was measured rather than assumed: stations x radialSegments x 2, so 11 x 14 x 2 = 308 triangles for the fan against the 15,748 already spent on the implicit surfaces.
geometryDescriptor.standProudNote: Runs BELOW the upper fan along its whole length -- 26 to 40 mm lower at every matching fore-aft station -- and roots inside the same pygostyle lobe. The two overlap as solids near the root and separate aft; they share no surface, so there is nothing co-facing to z-fight.

repetitionSystems.name: Eye pair
repetitionSystems.rationale: Two eyes are a mirrored pair, which a two-element radial ring about +Y expresses exactly. The emitter's perpendicular for axis (0,1,0) is (1,0,0) and it offsets by radius*0.5, so instance 0 lands at local +X 0.0165 and instance 1 at -X 0.0165: a true reflection with x negated and nothing else touched. One InstancedMesh, one draw call, one geometry, instead of two components against a unique-geometry ceiling of 16 that this prop sits one under.
repetitionSystems.placementNote: Parented to `head`, whose pivot was moved onto the measured pupil line specifically so this ring resolves to world (+/-0.0165, 0.531, 0.1023). The 0.0165 half-separation puts each 9.2 mm sphere just OUTSIDE the skull ellipsoid -- normalising against the skull's radii gives 1.03, so the eye sits proud of the surface rather than buried in it, and it is a sphere meeting a curved field, so there is no coincident co-facing pair.
repetitionSystems.costNote: MEASURED COST, recorded rather than optimised away because it cannot be optimised from here: this InstancedMesh is 2,432 triangles -- 1,216 per eye, for a sphere 9.2 mm across on a 0.55 m prop. That is 12 percent of the model's triangles for two of its smallest features. The repetition emitter builds its geometry with geometry_for(primitive, {}, False, seg) -- an EMPTY component -- so a repetition system has no geometryDescriptor and no way to ask for fewer segments; it gets the tier default, which for `standard` is a 32 x 20 sphere. The alternatives were weighed and refused: `capsule` is the primitive whose helper emits INVERTED WINDING (see thigh-l), and `box` or `instanced-cluster` would put a visible cube where the eye goes. Triangles are the axis with the most headroom here (20,516 of 32,000, 64 percent) while unique geometries sit at 16 of 16, so spending them on the eye is the right trade -- but it is a trade, and the number is written down rather than left to be discovered.

reviewHistory.summary: Interaction-pass. The runtime contract is built exactly as declared, and it is deliberately a SMALL contract. Measured off the built model: ONE pivot, the root at base-center; ZERO sockets; ONE collider, convex, on body-shell; ZERO destruction groups. That is the whole of it, and it is the right answer rather than a gap. This bird is authored in one fixed standing pose and thaikit's kit is static geometry with no rig and no animation, so nothing on it articulates and nothing attaches to it. A live rooster has a hock, a hip, a neck and a jaw, and giving each of them a pivot would have promised a game that those parts turn -- the sealed-oil-drum failure of describing a machine that does not exist. The collider is a single convex hull over the trunk: the tarsus is 13 mm thick and the tail is feathers, and neither earns its own proxy on a low-end target. The generator writes a colliders entry for every component including nulls, and the thaikit adapter prunes those, because a nameless empty proxy in the runtime list reads as a physics shape that exists and does nothing. Destruction groups are DERIVED from the built nodes rather than assumed empty, so a component that somehow carried a fractureGroup would fail promotion loudly instead of being silently dropped here. check_part_coverage: 15 specified, 16 built, 0 errors -- the extra is the instanced eye pair, correctly a detail group. The model is explodable and clickable through 16 named nodes.

reviewHistory.summary: Optimization-pass. All four axes measured off the built module: 20,516 triangles of 32,000, 16 draw calls of 24, 10 materials of 16, 16 unique geometries of 16, zero textures, and createObjectModel returns in about 710 ms. No geometry was changed in this pass because nothing was over; what it produced instead is three measured facts that were previously assumptions. First, the SDF resolution sweep in the blockout showed 44 and 52 returning identical geometry and I recorded that as saturating at 44 -- the real cap is 40, set by SDF_MAX_RESOLUTION on the standard tessellation tier that targetTriangles 32000 selects, so both values were being clamped and every resolution actually used here (24, 34, 36) is below it and real. Second, the eye pair costs 2,432 triangles, 1,216 for a sphere 9.2 mm across, which is 12 percent of the model's triangles for two of its smallest features; it cannot be reduced from the spec because the repetition emitter builds geometry from an EMPTY component and so has no way to ask for fewer segments, and the two cheaper primitives were refused on their merits -- capsule is the one with inverted winding and box would put a visible cube where the eye goes. Third, the 10 measured materials against 8 declared are not drift: createSculptMaterial gives every implicit-surface component its own instance, so body-shell, head, leg-l and leg-r each hold a dedicated copy of a material the sweeps share. Triangles are the axis with headroom at 64 percent; unique geometries are the binding one at exactly 16 of 16, and that ceiling shaped this prop from the blockout onward rather than at the end.

reviewHistory.summary: POST-SHIP CORRECTION: THE FEET WERE NOT ATTACHED. Reported by eye after promotion, then confirmed as a topology measurement rather than an impression -- welding vertices by position and counting connected components gave leg-l and leg-r TWO islands each, 867 vertices of tarsus and 754 of foot, where all fourteen other components are a single island. Cause: the ankle sphere sat at y 0.047 with radius 0.0085, bottoming out at 0.0385, while the toe capsules lay flat at y 0.011 topping out at 0.016. A 22.5 mm gap against a 4.5 mm smooth-union radius, so the field never joined and marching cubes correctly produced two surfaces. reviewHistory.summary: POST-SHIP CORRECTION 2 AND 3: THE LEGS WERE NOT JOINED TO THE BODY, AND THEN SHOWED A FLAT FACE. Both reported by eye, both then measured. Correction 2: the thigh root sat at y 0.205 while the body's surface at the thigh's own position is y 0.214 -- the bbox minimum of 0.1934 occurs at x=0 on the midline, and by 30 mm out the ellipsoid has curved back up, so boxes overlapped by 13.6 mm while surfaces grazed by 2.5. Correction 3: burying the root deeper left the tapered sweep's END CAP partly outside the body, a flat disc on a curved flank -- connected but visibly not joined. Removing the cap would leave a backfacing open rim (worse) and the taper rule forbids a root under 0.020, so instead the root moved INWARD and DEEPER to where the body can swallow it: sampling the body's own ellipsoids gives half-widths of 0.037 at y 0.228 but 0.040 at y 0.250, so the root rises to y 0.250 and moves in to x 0.010, and the sweep walks back out to x 0.030 as it descends. All 13 root-cap vertices now measure inside the body. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING WAS IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT. The new attachment checker used THREE.Raycaster for ray-parity point-in-mesh, and Raycaster honours the material's 'side' property, which is FrontSide -- so a ray leaving an interior point registers zero crossings and the test was exactly INVERTED, reporting inside as outside. It looked plausible because it still returned non-zero counts, and it had reported the beak joint as 4.6 mm. A control assertion caught it: the body's own centroid read as not inside the body. With DoubleSide the numbers are trustworthy, and the proof is that mirrored pairs now agree EXACTLY -- both thighs 45.3 mm, both wings 40.5 mm -- where before they differed 6.1 against 2.5. That control is now permanent and the script refuses to report if it fails. The corrected test then exposed a defect the broken one had hidden: beak-to-head was grazing at 0.4 mm, now 8.4 mm. The hock joint, marginal at 4.1 against 3.8 for a mirrored pair, is now 12.2 and 11.8. Every declared attachment measures at least 8.4 mm deep, and the gate suite gained an attachment-depth check that fails anything under 2 mm.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: All four ceilings come from thaikit's resolveBudget() for the `hero4x` class and none was invented. The BINDING axis here is maxUniqueGeometries, not triangles: the validator counts one geometry per component plus one per repetition system, so 14 components + 1 system = 15 against a ceiling of 16, while the triangle estimate of about 14,000 sits at 44% of its own ceiling. Every structural decision on this prop was made against that 16, in the blockout and not afterwards. Three of them cost real fidelity and are recorded as trades rather than as savings: the comb and wattle are folded into the head's implicit field instead of being their own components; all four toes, four claws and the spur are folded into each leg's implicit field; and the tail's ~14 individual feathers are built as two swept sheaves rather than fourteen cards. The last of these was forced rather than chosen -- the repetition-system emitter places instances evenly around a full circle and has no per-instance transform list, so a swept fan of feathers at fourteen different angles and lengths is not expressible as one InstancedMesh at all. textureSize is 0 because every material declares textureless.
performanceBudget.measuredNote:
MEASURED off the built module, not estimated: 20,516 triangles / 32,000, 16 draw calls / 24, 10 materials / 16, 16 unique geometries / 16, 0 textures, and createObjectModel returns in about 710 ms.
THE BINDING AXIS IS UNIQUE GEOMETRIES, at 16 of 16 exactly. Every structural decision on this prop was made against that number in the blockout rather than optimised toward it afterwards, and three of them cost real fidelity: the comb and wattle are folded into the head's implicit field instead of being their own components; all four toes, four claws and the spur are folded into each leg's field; and the tail is three swept sheaves rather than the plate's roughly fourteen separate feathers. The last was FORCED -- the repetition emitter places instances evenly around a full circle with no per-instance transform, so a swept fan cannot be an InstancedMesh.
MATERIALS READ 10 WHERE THE SPEC DECLARES 8, and the two extra are not spec drift. createSculptMaterial takes a denseComponent flag and gives every implicit-surface component its own instance: body-shell, head, leg-l and leg-r each hold a dedicated copy, while the eight sweep and capsule components share six. So plumage-dark, skin-red and leg-scale each exist twice on the GPU. Each duplicate is a real shader and render-state switch, and at 10 of 16 it is affordable, but it is measured and named rather than assumed to equal the spec count.
TIME TO PREVIEW is 710 ms, and essentially all of it is marching cubes over the four implicit fields -- every material declares textureless, so the five-canvas-per-material synthesis that costs seconds elsewhere in this kit costs nothing here. textureSize is 0 and the model uploads no textures at all.

lightingFromPhoto: KEY: upper front right, about 35 degrees azimuth and 40 degrees elevation, soft-edged. Confirmed by the flank reading about 12 luma below the breast, and by the key-side silhouette edge reading 113 luma against 24 just 8 px inside it -- a curving surface turning into the key, not an edge light.
FILL: broad and soft, from the backdrop, at roughly 0.45 of the key. The shadow side never drops below luma 10 anywhere on the bird.

RIM: NONE, and this is measured rather than assumed. Across 43 rows of the body the aft, shadow-side silhouette edge reads 25.3 luma against 25.0 eight pixels inside it -- a lift of 0.3, which is nothing. The only bright edge on the plate is on the KEY side and is the key itself. So no rim or kicker is declared, because adding one would be inventing a light the photograph does not contain, and it would wash out the near-black plumage that is identity-defining here.

ENVIRONMENT: a flat studio backdrop measuring rgb 157,157,157 with a standard deviation of 0.08, taken from a 12 px border ring rather than assumed -- a genuinely flat grey, not a white product matte. It behaves as a large low-intensity hemisphere and it is what fills the shadow side; it is the only environment contribution in the plate and there is no HDR content, no window and no coloured bounce to reproduce.

EXPOSURE AND TONE MAPPING: render at exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping. This matters more than usual on this prop and it was measured, not assumed: with the body's albedo the render's flank spanned a luma range of 6 to 10 against the plate's 10 to 36, so the tone curve was crushing the darks and the flank had no readable form. Four albedos were lifted in the material pass to compensate, and the median luma now tracks the plate within 3 levels on four of six materials.
No baked lighting and no ambient occlusion enters any base colour. Every albedo is de-lit and each records the method and the crop it came from.
proceduralStrategy: Implicit fields for everything continuous and organic: the trunk, the head, and each leg. Marching cubes over smooth-unioned ellipsoids, capsules and cones gives welded surfaces with no internal seams and therefore no coincident co-facing pairs to z-fight.

Tapered sweeps for everything that curves and narrows: neck, beak, both mantles, both wings, and both tail sheaves. It is the only primitive here that carries a curved spine AND a section closing to a true point.
One InstancedMesh for the eye pair, placed as a two-element radial ring about +Y, which the emitter renders as a true x-negated reflection.
Every material flat-albedo and textureless, with a measured colour and a measured roughness, and colorVariation carrying what a texture would otherwise carry.
Deterministic throughout: no procedural noise, no random seeds, nothing that renders differently twice.

materialPipeline.statusNote:
`proceed`, and the honest reading of every registryConfidence of 1.0 below is: I NAMED THE PROFILE, the tool did not measure it. The method on all seven is `explicit-material-id`, which means the id resolves in docs/materials/material-reference.json -- nothing more.
The first run of this manifest is preserved in the reasoning because it is the informative one. Left to resolve by family it returned `probe`: six regions fell back at confidences of 0.488 to 0.559, and the seventh, the bare comb and face skin, returned `request-input` outright rather than call a rooster's comb human skin. That refusal was correct. The registry carries fourteen families -- ceramic, coating, fabric, fur, gemstone, glass, hair, leather, metal, plastic, rubber, skin, stone, wood -- and NOT ONE of them is feather, beak or scute.
So the ids here are the nearest canonical profiles, chosen deliberately and named for what they are: `fur.stylized` for all three plumage materials, because a fibrous keratinous covering with a soft sheen and no specular lobe is the closest light transport the library has; `skin.human.code-only` for bare vascular avian skin, which differs from human skin in papillation and colour but not in family; `leather.matte` for beak and scute keratin, which is hard where leather is soft and is chosen for being a dielectric protein sheath rather than for feeling similar. The per-material materialClassConfidence values on spec.materials -- 0.40 to 0.90 -- are the honest numbers for how near these are, and they are deliberately NOT overwritten by the 1.0 here.
What actually determines every rendered value is the pixel evidence: seven crops, each visually confirmed on the surface it names, each returning `pass` from extract_pbr_evidence at confidence 0.751 to 0.860. Where a tool and the pixels disagree the pixels govern -- which is also why analyze_texture.py's finish classifier is refused outright in materialEvidenceReport.finishClassRejected, having called the tail feathers `candy-coat` at metalness 0.35.
